table_a_perception_ablation.description: Four melanoma-detection arms assembled from three already-written evidence artifacts. Primary numbers are the one-shot confirmatory test split (n=395); the matching valid-split (n=203) numbers from G6 are attached as a reference point, not a second endpoint.
table_a_perception_ablation.youden_j_formula: sensitivity + specificity - 1, recomputed here from each source's own rounded sens/spec
table_a_perception_ablation.youden_j_rounding_note: Recomputing from already-rounded (4dp) sensitivity/specificity can differ from a source file's own stored youden_j by up to 0.0001 (rounding order). E.g. criteria_path_alone test: 0.5743+0.8946-1=0.4689 here vs 0.4688 as stored in confirmatory_test_395.json. Immaterial, disclosed rather than silently reconciled.

contract_layer_context.note: safe_to_display / conflict / escalation / undecidable / citation rates are properties of the full decision-contract pipeline (classifier diagnosis + complete criteria table + guideline catalog) evaluated once on the confirmatory run. They are not computed per melanoma-detection arm below and do not vary across classifier-alone / criteria-alone / union / stacked, because none of those four variants is what the contract is built from -- every contract in the confirmatory run uses the classifier's committed diagnosis and the full seven-criterion table regardless of which of the four sensitivity/specificity numbers you are reading. Reported once here, attached to all four arms below as shared context rather than duplicated with false per-arm precision.

classifier_alone.description: Diagnosis classifier's own MEL prediction. Ranking score exists (posterior).

criteria_path_alone.auroc_note: No AUROC: 'seven-point score >= threshold' is a binary rule, not a ranked score to sweep.
criteria_path_alone.description: Seven-point checklist score (from trained criterion heads) >= threshold 3.

union_rule.auroc_note: No AUROC: 'classifier flags OR criteria flags' is a binary OR of two flags, not a ranked score.
union_rule.description: Flags melanoma if EITHER the classifier OR the criteria path does.

stacked_ensemble.description: Logistic-regression meta-learner over multi-view predictions, registered threshold 0.2981.
stacked_ensemble.disclosure: The confirmatory runner did not implement the registered stacked comparison; this module completes it on the same fitted readers and split. The union-rule outcome was already observed when this was computed, so the two are reported together and neither is presented as a blind result. The comparator's test metrics were also visible during design (see test_split_exposure in the preregistration).

table_b_system_ablation.description: Five run_cohort('valid') variants, computed fresh (not read from an existing artifact). Arm 1 is the real function call; arms 2-5 are new functions in this script that call build_contract/router/criterion_abstention differently, per the task's instruction not to modify run_cohort.py/contract.py/router.py/criterion_abstention.py themselves.

1_full_system.note: This IS run_cohort('valid'), unmodified. Flagged for arms 2 and 5 below: build_contract() calls catalog.bind(classifier_diagnosis) unconditionally on every case here -- medguard_v2/evidence/router.py is never imported by run_cohort.py -- and these criterion heads are argmax LogisticRegression classifiers that structurally cannot emit INDETERMINATE, since that label never appears in their training data -- medguard_v2/perception/criterion_abstention.py is never imported by run_cohort.py either (it is used exactly once in the package, by eval/agent_eval.py). So on the retrieval-gating and abstention dimensions specifically, this 'full system' arm already IS what arms 2 and 5 ask to ablate down to. Both arms report the real counterfactual (router-gated retrieval / policy-applied abstention) instead of a diff against itself.

2_no_router.note: 'No router' (always trigger retrieval) is what ships today -- see arm 1's note. This arm is therefore numerically identical to arm 1 on every field above retrieval_calls_as_shipped_ungated. 'retrieval_calls_if_gated_by_router' is the real counterfactual: running medguard_v2/evidence/router.route() against these same 203 contracts (same classifier_diagnosis/confidence/score, nothing refit). Gating mostly saves calls on NO_COVERAGE cases (NEV/SK/MISC, ~2/3 of valid), where build_contract issues a catalog.bind() that is known in advance to return nothing.

3_no_criteria.note: Every criterion is INDETERMINATE, so score_min=0 and score_max=10=MAX_SCORE for all 203 cases: the checklist can never clear the threshold (score_min>=3) and can never rule it out (score_max<3), so undecidable_rate above is exactly 1.0 by construction -- this is the intended, not a bug. citation_rate is unchanged from the full system because guideline binding follows classifier_diagnosis only, never the criteria table; contingent guidance drops from the full system's count to 0, because it requires the checklist to affirmatively flag melanoma (score_min>=3), which is now impossible. DESIGN INCONSISTENCY SURFACED BY THIS ABLATION: conflict_rate/escalation_rate above (from DecisionContract.conflict, contract.py's own _build_conflict) equal classifier_predicts_mel_rate, because contract.py flags a conflict whenever the classifier says MEL and score_min<3 -- it does not check score.decidable, so 'checklist never actually assessed this' and 'checklist actively disagrees' both count as the same kind of conflict there. router_state_distribution above tells a different story: it is 100% UNDECIDABLE and 0% CONFLICT, because router.classify_state() additionally requires score.decidable before it will call something a CONFLICT (see router.py's classify_state, the classifier==MEL branch). Two modules in this codebase both compute 'is this a conflict' and disagree once criteria go indeterminate; it is invisible on the full system (undecidable_rate 0.0000 there) and only shows up under this ablation.

score_disagrees_with_its_own_criteria_ta.how_it_was_produced: dataclasses.replace(contract, score=<score of a different criteria table>)
verification_failures: score does not match the criteria table it claims to summarise
guideline record aad:pmid:29331385:table-vii-low-risk-excision failed its content hash

4_no_contracts.note: Measured effect on this cohort: 0 additional cases would display if verification_failures() were skipped -- the check never fires through the normal build_contract() path, because build_contract's own score always matches the criteria table it just computed, guideline hashes are pre-verified once at GuidelineCatalog.load() (a tampered record raises GuidelineIntegrityError there, before any contract exists), and _build_conflict() never returns present=True with an empty description. It is a defense-in-depth invariant on this pipeline, not an active filter -- '0 change' is the correct measurement, not a null result. adversarial_demonstrations above shows the check is not vacuous in general: each demo takes a real contract and corrupts it the same way the project's own test suite does (dataclasses.replace, which build_contract() itself cannot produce), and the check catches all three. Skipping verification would let each one display.

as_literally_named_no_abstention.note: Identical to arm 1 -- see arm 1's note. Restated here so this arm is self-contained.

real_counterfactual_with_fitted_policy_a.policy_source: research/evidence/derm7pt_v1/criterion_abstention_v1.json (fit on train, out-of-fold; loaded, not refit)

5_no_abstention.note: Per-criterion: argmax accuracy on the subset each head abstains on vs. the subset it keeps, both computed against Derm7pt's real per-criterion gold labels (not a proxy). Case level: the melanoma-threshold verdict (score>=3) compared against gold seven_point_score>=3, which schema.py's own docstring states this checklist reproduces on 1011/1011 Derm7pt cases, so it is exact ground truth here, not recomputed by this script. 'argmax_forced_verdict_error_rate_on_cases_abstention_would_flag_undecidable' vs '..._overall' is the key comparison: if the first is higher, abstention is concentrating on exactly the cases the forced argmax verdict gets wrong, i.e. buying real safety rather than just adding caution.

integration_findings: medguard_v2/evidence/router.py (gated retrieval: NO_COVERAGE/CONFLICT/UNDECIDABLE/ROUTINE) is fully implemented but not imported anywhere in the executed pipeline -- not by run_cohort.py, not by eval/confirmatory.py, not by eval/agent_eval.py, not by agent/clinician_agent.py. Verified by grep across medguard_v2/**/*.py: the only hit is the module's own definition. run_cohort's shipped behaviour already matches what arm 2 ('no router') was specified to be.

medguard_v2/perception/criterion_abstention.py (margin-based INDETERMINATE producer, policy already fit on train) is used in exactly one place in the whole package: eval/agent_eval.py. run_cohort.py's criterion heads are plain LogisticRegression.predict() calls, which cannot emit a class absent from their training labels, so run_cohort's undecidable_rate is structurally 0.0000 -- confirmed both by criterion_abstention.py's own docstring and by direct measurement here. run_cohort's shipped behaviour already matches what arm 5 ('no abstention') was specified to be.

contract.py's DecisionContract.conflict (_build_conflict) and router.py's classify_state() both compute 'is this case a conflict' and disagree once criteria go indeterminate: _build_conflict only checks score_min>=threshold, so classifier=MEL + an unassessed checklist reads as a conflict; classify_state additionally requires score.decidable, so the same case reads as UNDECIDABLE, not CONFLICT. Invisible on the shipped pipeline (undecidable_rate 0.0000 there); visible and quantified under arm 3 (no_criteria) above, where conflict_rate/escalation_rate (contract.py's definition) and router_state_distribution (router.py's definition) tell different stories about the same 203 contracts.
